stories.title: Cyber attack ruled out by UK's NATS as flights resume
stories.summary: The head of the UK's air traffic control provider has ruled out a cyber attack as the cause of technical issues which grounded flights yesterday. Airlines in the UK are continuing to deal with the knock-on impacts with some disruption expected to affect airports including Heathrow, Gatwick, Manchester and Stansted. Fight schedules are also returning to normal in Ireland following disruption to dozens of incoming and outgoing flights at Cork, Dublin and Shannon airports yesterday. Around 90 flights to and from Dublin Airport were cancelled yesterday due to the issue. The UK's air traffic control provider, NATS, said the problem has since been resolved. NATS chief executive Martin Rolfe is due to speak to Britain's Transport Secretary regarding the technical issue.

stories.title: Number of Irish flights cancelled over UK technical issue
stories.summary: A number of flights departing from and arriving into Irish airports have been cancelled due to air traffic control issues in the UK, which have since been resolved. A large number of departing flights at major British airports were disrupted after air traffic control ⁠provider Nats experienced a technical issue. Nats said the "system issue" had been resolved at about 7.30pm. "We are operating normally and working as hard as possible to clear the backlog of flights," it said in a statement on X. Flight tracking website FlightRadar24 said that almost 1,100 flights to and from UK airports were cancelled. It said that by 8pm, a total of 1,055 flights had been cancelled. More than 70 flights, inbound and outbound, were cancelled at Dublin Airport. As of 7pm this evening, Dublin Airport said that 43 departures and 30 arrivals were cancelled.

stories.title: Further fuel price measures may be needed, says Taoiseach
stories.summary: Taoiseach Micheál Martin has intimated there may be a need for further measures to help combat the rising prices of petrol and diesel. The Fianna Fáil leader was speaking on the second day of his party's annual think-in Tullamore after the lobby group Fuels for Ireland last week claimed diesel prices had risen to about €2 a litre in some forecourts. Mr Martin refused to rule out a further subsidy for fuel after the Coalition last month moved to extend excise cuts - introduced in the Spring - until November amid the ongoing blockage of the Strait of Hormuz with no resolution to the US-Iran war in sight. "We have to look at that and we are discussing that in the next two to three weeks in terms of the overall picture. "That’s notwithstanding if there was a breakthrough in talks between the United States and Iran and the Middle East more generally. So, we have to factor all of that that in." The Cork South Central TD rejected an assertion he had given in to the demands of April’s fuel protesters or that he had prioritised their demands over doing more to help people with rising household bills.

stories.title: Brent crude rises above $100 a barrel as war escalates
stories.summary: Benchmark Brent crude oil futures rose past $100 a barrel this morning, breaching the symbolic barrier for the first time since July 24 as intensifying conflict in the Middle East fuelled growing concern about oil flows from the region. Brent crude futures rose $2.15, or 2.2%, to $100.07 a barrel this morning, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was up $1.70, or 1.83%, at $94.73 a barrel. Brent crude prices have risen by a quarter since early last month as hopes fade for a permanent resolution to the six-month-old US-Iran conflict. This week, attacks by Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi energy facilities set oil installations ablaze, threatening a significant expansion of the conflict. The Houthi attacks could threaten crude shipments via the Red Sea, which has been a key alternative route to the crucial Strait of Hormuz, where crude flows have been severely curtailed since the February 28 start of the Iran war. A growing number of banks, including Goldman Sachs, Bank of America and HSBC, have raised their crude price forecasts in recent days.

stories.title: Argentina targets energy firm over Falklands operation
stories.summary: Argentina's government has said it will file criminal charges ⁠against energy company Navitas Petroleum and its executives for operating in the Falkland Islands. The move follows remarks on Friday by Argentine President Javier Milei, who vowed to sanction oil companies drilling in the British overseas territory as he stepped up the South American nation's sovereignty claims. According ‌to a statement ⁠from the presidency, Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno will file the criminal complaint against several Navitas subsidiaries and partners operating in the territory, along with their corporate directors. The government alleges the firms violated Argentine law ⁠by holding hydrocarbon exploration and exploitation licences issued by ‌the UK in the North Falkland Basin. Mr Milei ⁠last week ‌singled out the Sea Lion offshore oil project as he announced measures targeting companies involved in Falklands oil and gas activities, ⁠with penalties potentially extending to shareholders, directors and suppliers. The Sea ⁠Lion field is operated by Tel Aviv-listed Navitas Petroleum, which holds a 65% stake.

stories.title: Parrott marks Champions League debut with goal for Betis
stories.summary: Troy Parrott marked his Champions League debut with a goal as Real Betis earned a 3-2 win at ten-man Lille. Only four days after netting his first Betis goal - a home winner against Real Madrid in La Liga - the Republic of Ireland striker was at it again, scoring what proved to be the winning goal eight minutes after half-time. Betis defender Marc Bartra had scored twice either side of half-time to cancel out goals from Ayase Ueda and Alexsandro Ribeiro before Parrott pounced. With the scores locked at 2-2, the Dubliner latched onto a through ball from Rodrigo Riquelme, made space for himself in the Lille box, before firing a low shot beyond the outstretched leg of Berke Ozer. Three minutes later, Ethan Mbappe, brother of Real Madrid and France striker Kylian, was sent off for Lille with Betis holding out for victory on their return to the Champions League stage after two decades. Parrott started the opening league phase game of this season's competition at the Stade Pierre-Mauroy and played the full 90 minutes plus stoppage time.

stories.title: McGuinness to stay in Donegal hot seat for 2027
stories.summary: Jim McGuinness will remain in the Donegal hot seat for 2027 after being reappointed as manager of the county's senior footballers on Monday night. McGuinness returned to inter-county management in 2023 on a three-year term, with the option for a fourth year. The county board has now confirmed he will be staying for another campaign, releasing a short statement that read: "Following a meeting of the County Committee, CLG Dhún na nGall confirm the appointment of Michael McCann as senior hurling manager for a two-year term and Jim McGuinness as senior football manager for a one-year term." McCann is heading into his 10th season in charge of the hurlers. He is the second longest serving manager in inter-county hurling, behind only Limerick's John Kiely. McGuinness famously guided Donegal to an All-Ireland SFC title in 2012. He also won Ulster crowns in 2011, 2012 and 2014 during his first term. stories.title: Iraola: Atletico test a gauge of Liverpool's level
stories.summary: Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola believes his managerial Champions League debut at home to Atletico Madrid will provide a good indication of the level his side are at. A first win of the season on Friday against promoted Ipswich cannot be considered a genuine barometer of how well the team have adapted to the change of style implemented by the Basque since he replaced Arne Slot in the summer. It will also be a test of Iraola's own credentials as he has never coached at this level, having featured in just three matches in Europe’s elite club competition as a player for Athletic Bilbao. Liverpool faced Atletico at home in last season’s Champions League opener, registering their third successive victory over Diego Simeone’s side – Virgil van Dijk’s stoppage-time goal securing the win after the Reds had relinquished a 2-0 lead. "Obviously it is a special night for me; everyone talks about Champions League nights at Anfield," Iraola said. "It’s one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to put myself in the position that I am right now and I hope I can enjoy it.

stories.title: Round up: Ulster and Connacht bag first pre-season wins
stories.summary: Ulster and Connacht recorded their first pre-season victories in two tense tussles over the weekend. On Friday night, Richie Murphy's Ulster scraped past fellow URC challengers Edinburgh in Scotland, three weeks prior to their opening league clash on 25 September. As for Connacht, they were big winners over English CHAMP side Ealing Trailfinders, whose squad featured four Irish players. Ulster got their pre-season campaign off to an ideal start with a narrow two-point victory over Edinburgh in the Hive Stadium on Friday night. Debutant half-backs Jamie Benson and Matthew Devine combined for 11 points, with the former Connacht man scoring a first-half try, as Ulster raced into a 14 point lead after just 25 minutes. With a 27-man travelling squad named by Richie Murphy, all eyes were on the plentiful supply of new faces. Benson and Devine combined at half-back, Daniel Hawkshaw and Chay Mullins also started in the backline with Eduardo Bello, Ben Donnell, Eli Snyman and Martin Moloney all among the replacements. Academy prospects Flynn Longstaff and Jed Findlay rounded off the debutants from the bench also. The visitors raced into an early lead helped by set-piece dominance. A scrum penalty win led to the first try, with hooker James McCormick dotting down from the back of a powerful rolling maul. Edinburgh responded with a try of their own courtesy of centre Geordie Gwynn, but then came Ulster's gear change.

stories.title: Something for the Weekend: Xnthony's cultural picks
stories.summary: Award-winning musical theatre creator Xnthony returns this month with a new show about miracles and the people who stage them. Lourdes! The Musical is an electrifying pilgrimage of Hail Marys mixed with original pop bangers - the show premieres at Dublin Theatre Festival this September and October. Steel Magnolias - We lost a great with Dolly's recent passing. So, in her honour, my fella suggested we watch the classic that is Steel Magnolias. This adaptation of the great play absolutely floored me. It reminds me so much of Lourdes! The Musical!, my new show. It is quite happy to saunter along with cheeriness, wit and a sense of fun, and then suddenly the knife twists and you are absolutely in bits. It brings all the feels, but constantly undercuts them with humour and genuinely laugh out loud put downs. These characters love each other, but they’re not afraid to have their opinions heard! I love that it is an adaptation of a play too. The dialogue is whip smart, the characters are brilliantly drawn, and its heart is completely undeniable. Like every other gay right now, I have also been completely lost in the world of Madonna’s Confessions II. I am OBSESSED with the first five songs in particular. A masterclass in segues, spoken word and killer pop hooks.

stories.title: The Traitors Ireland: Saving your best/worst until last
stories.summary: There were plenty of tears but not too many laughs as the current series of The Traitors Ireland reached the halfway point on Tuesday night. After banishing two Traitors - Fionula and Páraic K on consecutive nights, The Faithfuls were going for the hat-trick. ***Warning: Spoilers for The Traitors Ireland episode six below*** When told by Traitor Carla that she could either join her or be murdered on the spot, Aoife didn't hesitate: a cloak in the castle beat a cab back home. "I've always wanted to wear that cloak," Aoife admitted, "and this is my only opportunity. I would kick myself if I let her (Carla) murder me to my face like that. I couldn't do it." And with that, we were off to the races. Again. Having drawn "so much heat" when she was a Faithful, Aoife said she wanted "heat for a reason now" - and unwittingly got just that the morning after her change of heart. Talking theories with David, Janet, and Kayleigh, Aoife said, "We - they - murdered Saoirse..." Kayleigh and David copped the slip of the tongue, and Aoife's chances of surviving until the next morning took another hit. Mind you, as the day progressed, it looked like David would be giving Aoife a run for her money... One of the best team players of the series so far, the beady-eyed (and behatted) Denis felt like the favourite to be murdered after losing out on a shield in Monday's mission. Sure enough, Carla and Aoife agreed that he was too much of a danger to their respective paths to the final. And so, Denis was dispatched with ruthless efficiency, leaving husband Diego heartbroken and the rest of Team Faithful one sage short.

stories.summary: A garda investigation is under way into reports of a large unidentified drone flying off the east coast, just days before the visit of US President Donald Trump to Ireland. At around 5pm yesterday a pilot flying a commercial aircraft towards Dublin Airport reported seeing a large drone off the coast of Co Wicklow. Other pilots who were in the air at the time were alerted to the possible presence of the drone over the Irish Sea. AirNav Ireland - the semi-state company responsible for receiving reports of aviation safety occurences - has confirmed that an aircraft arriving into Dublin yesterday reported a possible drone sighting. In line with its normal safety procedures, a safety report has been filed and the sighting was reported to An Garda Síochána. AirNav said as this matter is now with the relevant authorities, it cannot comment further at this time.

stories.summary: Gardaí are understood to be investigating whether a 17-year-old boy who died in a hit-and-run incident in Co Clare may have had some interaction with a group of others in the time immediately preceding his death. Bryan Lowe sustained fatal injuries following an incident near Clonlara, close to the Clare/Limerick border late on Friday night. Emergency services were alerted after he was found unresponsive at Cottage Cross, near Clonlara. Bryan had been on a scrambler e-bike. A silver/gold coloured Skoda Octavia believed to have been involved in the collision did not remain at the scene. Bryan's mother, Crystal Lowe, said she and his two sisters are "devastated" and added that "Bryan will be sadly missed". Detectives have appealed to any road users with dash-cam footage, who were in the Clonlara/Castleconnell area on Friday night, to contact them.

stories.title: Budget proposals may swing to fairway or bunker for Govt
stories.summary: Some members of the Fianna Fáil parliamentary party gathered in a pub co-owned by local golfing legend Shane Lowry on Sunday evening ahead of the party's two-day annual think-in in Tullamore. Ministers are now at the point where some proposals for October's Budget are set to land on the fairway while others fall off into the bunker. The Government's decision to extend temporary fuel excise cuts until the end of October at an estimated cost of €407m has left the Coalition with less wriggle room to deliver on all the budgetary promises it has floated in recent months, with the Opposition putting the pressure on to do more to help people with the cost of living. With that in mind, the Taoiseach was emphatic ahead of his party's think-in that there would be no return of universal energy credits. "The sort of energy credits for everybody, I can't see the capacity being there to do that", said Micheál Martin said. The Coalition is pressing ahead with income tax cuts with Minister for Finance Simon Harris stating the Budget would help people "who get up early every morning and go to work".

stories.title: Inditex reports profit miss despite strong August sales
stories.summary: Zara owner Inditex reported weaker than expected second-quarter profit today as costs increased due to the Middle East conflict, driving its shares down 3% despite a strong start to autumn trading. The fast-fashion group reported currency-adjusted sales up 9% in August, in a sign that extreme heat across Europe had not deterred shoppers. Inditex made €11 billion in sales in its May to July second quarter, a resilient performance in the face of high energy prices and weak consumer sentiment during the intensifying Iran war. But its second-quarter gross profit margin was 56.7%, slightly below analysts' expectations, as the conflict increased costs. "Disruptions in the Middle East resulted in higher transport costs and input costs during the first half of the year," Inditex chief financial officer Andres Sanchez Iglesias told analysts on a call. The war is impacting Inditex's sales in the Middle East, though this has improved since the first quarter, said investor relations head Gorka Garcia-Tapia Yturriaga. Inditex has around 480 stores in the region operated by franchisees.

stories.title: Negotiators may meet again soon for talks - Zelensky
stories.summary: Russian, Ukrainian and US negotiators could meet as early as this month for talks on finding an end to the war, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said, hours after Moscow pounded Kyiv with missiles and drones. The overnight barrage killed three people, the capital's mayor said, sending smoke billowing above the city as Moscow ended its temporary halt to strikes on Kyiv. US President Donald Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner had visited the Russian and Ukrainian capitals at the weekend for talks with both Mr Zelensky and Russian President Vladimir Putin. There was no immediate breakthrough in the bid to end Europe's deadliest conflict since World War II, but Mr Zelensky said there were hopes to resume direct talks between Russia and Ukraine in the coming weeks. "All of us will be preparing and bringing closer a trilateral meeting between Ukraine, Russia, and America," Mr Zelensky told journalists. "If all sides agree, we also want to hold it in the autumn. If September works out, then it would be great.

stories.title: Brennan: 'Men or women, it doesn't make a difference'
stories.summary: Sligo woman Nicola Brennan says the Melvin Gaels players "couldn't care less" about the gender of their manager after her appointment at the Leitrim club last weekend. Mick Calvey's mid-championsip departure left a void the Kinlough outfit moved swiftly to fill. Brennan was asked to take the reins last Thursday. After mulling it over for 24 hours, she took the gig, meeting with the players on Saturday before starting preparations for this weekend's round 4 intermediate clash against Aughavas. A female manager taking over a men's Gaelic football team is unusual but not unprecedented. Ocean FM report that Maureen McTernan managed the Glencar/Manorhamilton junior men's team back in 1999, while Cailin Molloy took charge of Co Down club Ballykinlar in 2017. Brennan herself is steeped in football. She represented the Yeats County with aplomb, and is still lining out for her club Tourlestrane. Her father Anthony Brennan is a hugely experienced manager who helmed Sligo men's under-21s, minors and under-16s, Sligo IT, as well as his own club Tourelstrane and Longford side Fr Manning Gaels.

stories.title: Mac Allister 'very sad' not to be offered new Reds deal
stories.summary: Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister admits he could have left in the summer as he was "sad" the club had not offered him a new contract when other players were having deals renewed. Fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch both had their stays extended, but Mac Allister said his agent was told the club was "not in a position" to offer him one. Admittedly, the Argentina international had not had his best season, with doubts expressed about whether he still had the legs for the Premier League, but that could have been said about the majority of Arne Slot's title winners who put up a dismal defence. Mac Allister was linked with a summer move, including to Wednesday’s Champions League opponents Atletico Madrid, but he still has two years remaining on his current deal and wanted to stay as he believes the team can still be successful. "I think as everyone knows I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract, which of course makes me very, very sad. "I think I give 100% for this football club every single day in training, games. Of course I can have very good games, bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

stories.title: Refreshed Van der Flier ready for World Cup year
stories.summary: Leinster and Ireland flanker Josh van der Flier knows that nothing is won in early September, but that doesn't mean that the 2027 Rugby World Cup escapes the imagination ahead of the start of the 2026/27 season. Speaking at the launch of the IRFU’s new men’s and women’s national team jerseys at the Guinness Open Gate Brewery this week, the 33-year-old was in fine form, which could be attributed to a healthy body and mind. "(I’m) feeling fit as well and getting back into a bit of pre-season stuff and ready for a big few months." This optimistic outlook will come as soothing words to head coach Andy Farrell, who prepares his 12-month plan where all roads hopefully lead to a World Cup final in Sydney on Saturday, 13 November. Van der Flier was part of the two most recent touring squads to Japan in 2019 and France in 2023, where both Irish efforts were ended by the All Blacks. There is a feeling of now or never ahead of the next edition however, but van der Flier insists that he is taking the coming months one at a time. "It's always tempting to start thinking of those (major tournaments), but it's obviously like how rugby goes, it tends to be week-to-week and you've got to look after your pre-season first," he said.

stories.title: Review: MG's S6 spacious family SUV
stories.summary: Irish car buyers have certainly embraced the crossover concept that makes many cars look like SUV's, even when they are only vaguely related, and manufacturers continue to meet the demand with more and more of them. The latest to come our way is the Chinese MG S6, which may lack the presence of a VW ID4, the sharp looks of a Skoda Enyaq or the bold design of a Kia EV 6, but it does have a shape that more than meets most peoples’ expectations and there’s nothing to dislike. Like other Chinese cars, it offers a very attractive package in terms of - you’ve guessed it - price and standard equipment. However, the MG offers one more advantage - space and lots of it. The front and back offer seriously good head and legroom and the cabin has a spacious and bright aspect. But for the rather large centre console (it houses the gearshift dial and phone charger) between the driver and passenger seat, the S6 offers excellent levels of comfort and the car has benefited from the use of premium-looking materials in the main. The entry-level version comes in at just under €40,000, which presents a challenge for its big name competitors. The MGS6 EV Exclusive Long Range version has more standard equipment and advanced features, such as the panoramic sunroof.

stories.title: GAA rejects misogyny accusations after McAleese quits
stories.summary: GAA director general Tom Ryan has rejected accusations of misogyny "in the strongest possible terms" after it was revealed the integration of Gaelic games' three bodies will not happen in 2027. Ryan said a failure to reach agreement on "organisational structures" is the main reason behind the delay in the process. Dr Mary McAleese, the former President of Ireland, yesterday stood down as chairperson of the Integration Committee overseeing the amalgamation of the GAA, LGFA and Camogie Association. McAleese cited changes to agreed timelines, a GAA management committee that she described as "less than impressive", and her feeling that there were "people who are not entirely happy about the idea of including women in decision-making at the top level of Gaelic sports" who were holding the process back. "I can't accept that, I would refute that in the strongest possible terms," Ryan said when asked about accusations that the delays are built on misogyny. "I accept in the course of a project like this, there will be different perspectives and different points of view, and that's fine.

stories.summary: A Dublin-based recruitment consultancy firm has topped the latest Tax Defaulters' List from Revenue, with a total bill of just under €4.15m. When €621,648 was added in penalties and more than €1.1m in interest, the amount owed to Revenue rose to €4,147,088. The total amount remains unpaid, with Allen Recruitment Consulting now in liquidation. The case was one of four included in the latest Tax Defaulters' List that involved sums of more than €1m. The latest list also includes a Belfast-based events concession provider, Central Fusion Limited, which is based at the Innovation Centre on the Queens Rd.

stories.title: Summer passenger records broken at Dublin Airport
stories.summary: Dublin Airport said today that August was another record-breaking month for it as a total of 3.8 million passengers passed throught the airport - a 1% increase on the same month last year. The airport said the busy August added to what was its busiest ever summer, with just over 11.3 million passengers travelling through - an additional 198,000 or 1.8% increase on the same time last year. Every day in June, July and August saw more than 100,000 passengers at Dublin Airport, it noted. The busiest day in August was Sunday, August 16, when 134,700 passengers went through the airport, making it Dublin Airport's third-busiest day ever. Four of the airport's ten busiest days ever were recorded during August. Gary McLean, Managing Director of Dublin Airport, said that August was the 17th consecutive month of growth in passenger numbers for the airport. He said that after several months of work and a significant investment by airport operator daa, an overhaul of the security entry point in Terminal 2 has seen the introduction of new electronic boarding pass scanners.

stories.title: Netanyahu denies he was warned about 7 October attacks
stories.summary: Israeli opposition leaders have called Prime Minister Mr Netanyahu unfit to serve after a report that the United Arab Emirates had warned him before the 7 October, 2023 Hamas attack. Haaretz newspaper, in a report excerpted from a forthcoming book by its reporters, said UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan spoke to Mr Netanyahu a week and a half before the attack and told him that Hamas was planning a major operation. Mr Netanyahu's office called the report by the left-leaning newspaper "an absolute lie" and denied he spoke to the Emirati leader at that time. Gadi Eisenkot, a former military commander who has emerged as Netanyahu's top rival in upcoming 27 October elections, accused the long-serving prime minister of evading responsibility for security lapses and resorting to "pathetic" excuses, such as saying he was not woken up soon enough on the morning of the attack. "Netanyahu received dozens of warnings for 7 October and ignored them all. He is unfit," Mr Eisenkot wrote on X. Naftali Bennett, a former prime minister also running in elections, said Mr Netanyahu "bears personal and direct responsibility" for the deaths on 7 October, the deadliest attack in Israeli history.

stories.title: New hurling amendments to be trialled in Fitzgibbon Cup
stories.summary: A series of hurling rule amendments are set for use in the Fitzgibbon Cup league games, on recommendation from the GAA's hurling expert advisory group. The main amendments will see the banning of two consecutive hand-passes – a free being awarded to the opposition from the point where the second hand-pass was attempted – and an increase to six steps allowed for players in possession. Hand-passes, meanwhile, will also now require a "clear and definite striking action of a hand." Line umpires will be given stronger power to act on indiscretions while players contesting throw-ins must clash with a ground stroke and failure to do so will result in a free to the opposition. All other players are required to remain 13 metres back. Puck-outs must also cross the 45-metre line before being played by the defending team while '65s’ will now move back to be taken from the 65m-line in the opposition half. Sideline cuts that go over the bar without a touch from another attacking player will be worth two points. The group, chaired by John Meyler, were appointed by GAA President Jarlath Burns in March with their first meeting held in April.
